Explanation: A completed ride is the core value unit: a rider requests transport, Lyft matches the request with available supply, and the trip is completed from pickup to destination.
Lyft owns and operates the platform that connects riders with drivers, coordinates matching and pricing, processes transactions and sets the rules for participation.
Lyft has to keep enough riders and drivers active in each local market so that riders can get a car quickly and drivers can find paid trips without too much waiting.
Lyft benefits when more trips are completed and when riders and drivers keep returning to the marketplace.
Ride demand and driver supply can change quickly by place and time. Lyft also has to operate under different transport, labor, safety and pricing rules across markets.
Lyft coordinates the trip and earns revenue mainly from fees connected to rides and other platform services.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Request / Pay — The rider asks for a trip and pays through Lyft or another supported payment method. | → Provider · Trip Offer — Lyft sends trip opportunities to available drivers based on location and marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Match / Trip Info — Lyft shows the rider the matched driver or vehicle, pickup information and trip details. | → Provider · Payout — Lyft coordinates driver earnings and settlement after completed rides.

Explanation: Lyft sets platform rules for driver eligibility, vehicle requirements, conduct, ratings, safety, payments and how rides are offered, subject to local law.
The Lyft app remains the main access point, while partnerships with other companies can also bring riders into the platform through rewards, memberships and linked offers.
Lyft runs the apps, predicts demand, matches riders and drivers, shows trip information, supports users, coordinates payments and manages marketplace quality and safety.
Important resources include the rider and driver base, trip and location data, matching technology, payments infrastructure, the Lyft brand and partner relationships.
People use Lyft when they want transport from one place to another and prefer an on-demand ride over driving themselves or arranging another option.
Riders want to get from pickup to destination without having to find, call or negotiate with a driver themselves.
The app can show ride options, estimated pickup information and trip details so transportation can be arranged quickly.
Riders may face higher prices at busy times, longer waits when few drivers are nearby, cancellations, service problems or safety concerns.
The rider requests a trip, confirms the pickup and destination and pays through the platform or another supported method.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Request / Pay — The rider asks for a trip and pays through Lyft or another supported payment method. | ← Owner · Match / Trip Info — Lyft shows the rider the matched driver or vehicle, pickup information and trip details. | ← Provider · Ride — The driver performs the physical transport from pickup to destination. | ← Partner · Benefits / Access — Demand partners give their own customers benefits, rewards or linked offers that can lead them to use Lyft.

Explanation: A ride depends on whether Lyft operates in the location, whether eligible supply is available and whether the requested ride type can be served.
Riders usually request rides in the Lyft app, while partner programs can create additional reasons or pathways to use Lyft.
Riders choose a ride option, request pickup, take the trip, pay and can rate the experience afterward.
Riders bring trip demand, pickup and destination information, payment details, ratings and repeated usage that help create local demand density.
Drivers are the people who make their time and an eligible vehicle available to complete ride requests on the Lyft platform.
Drivers want access to nearby trip demand so they can turn available driving time and a vehicle into earnings.
Lyft can provide ride requests without drivers having to find each passenger themselves, while drivers can choose when to be available subject to local rules.
Drivers may spend time waiting between trips and must manage costs such as fuel or charging, insurance, maintenance, rental or financing.
Drivers receive ride offers, see trip and earnings information where available, decide whether to accept and complete the transport.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Trip Offer — Lyft sends trip opportunities to available drivers based on location and marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Ride — The driver performs the physical transport from pickup to destination. | ← Owner · Payout — Lyft coordinates driver earnings and settlement after completed rides.

Explanation: Drivers must satisfy local age, licensing, background-check and vehicle requirements before they can provide rides.
Drivers use Lyft's driver app to go online, receive trip requests, navigate to pickup and manage rides and earnings.
Drivers make themselves available, accept suitable trips, travel to pickup, transport riders and manage ratings and support issues.
Drivers contribute their time, local mobility capacity, driving skills and access to an eligible vehicle and required documents.
Companies such as Chase, DoorDash and United Airlines connect their own customers, members or rewards programs with Lyft and can create additional reasons to use the ride-hailing platform.
Demand partners help channel existing customers or members toward Lyft through benefits, rewards, integrations or joint offers.
Partners can make their own products or memberships more useful by adding transportation benefits, while deepening engagement with their customers.
Partnerships have to create enough value for both sides while managing technical integration, promotion costs, customer experience and changing commercial terms.
Partners provide rewards, memberships, linked accounts or promotional access that can lead customers to use Lyft rides.
Transaction Flows: → Consumer · Benefits / Access — Demand partners give their own customers benefits, rewards or linked offers that can lead them to use Lyft.

Explanation: A useful partner needs a customer base, product or membership that fits Lyft's users and can create enough incremental demand to justify integration.
Partner apps, memberships, loyalty programs and co-branded offers connect their users with Lyft.
Partners design benefits, communicate offers, link accounts and promote Lyft usage to their customers or members.
Partners contribute existing customer relationships, distribution channels, loyalty programs and promotional reach.
